contract:
Issue #4 Done when: given a position, returns the moves club players chose, how often, how each scored, plus the opening name; responses cached 30 days so each position is fetched once; if Lichess is slow, down or rate-limiting the answer is out of book and the game carries on (no crash); the token comes from LICHESS_TOKEN, never from code; tests pass in CI.

Architecture §3.2: ExplorerClient.lookup(fen, { ratings, speeds }); SQLite cache keyed by (fen, ratings, speeds), 30 days; one request at a time; 401 throws a configuration error with a clear message; 429 honors Retry-After and that lookup is out of book; 5xx or network error is out of book. Lichess JSON parsed with zod into our own ExplorerResult.

Designed types: ExplorerMove { uci, san, games, white, draws, black, averageRating }; OutOfBookReason = rate_limited|server_error|network|timeout|bad_response; ExplorerResult { moves sorted by games desc, totalGames = white+draws+black, opening {eco,name}|null, unavailable? (then moves [] and totalGames 0) }; unavailable results never cached; concurrent lookups serialised and same-key lookups deduplicated; token never logged or included in errors; src reads no env or .env; no new dependencies (node:sqlite, zod only); no live network in tests.

The spoke reported these deliberate choices (judge them): cache key uses the first four FEN fields; cache hits bypass the queue; unmapped HTTP statuses (400/403/404) give bad_response; fixture rows other than g6 were reconstructed from spike percentages. Coordinator gate on 3c182c8: pnpm test 6 files 55 passed, pnpm typecheck clean.
